audit_title: CRISPR Guide AI Locus-Grouped vs Gene-Grouped Validation Integrity Audit

HeLa.spatial_leakage_assessment: Minimal impact (Delta r = -0.0032). Sequence features generalize robustly across distinct 50-kb genomic windows in genome-wide screens.

HCT116.spatial_leakage_assessment: Negligible impact (Delta r = +0.0038). No evidence of optimistic bias from spatial proximity.

HL60.spatial_leakage_assessment: Negligible impact (Delta r = +0.0097). Grouped performance slightly exceeds random CV due to partition variance.

A375.statistical_infeasibility_rationale: A standard 10-fold gene-grouped cross-validation requires at least 10 independent gene groups. Because the Doench 2016 A375 dataset targets only 8 unique genes, a 10-fold split would result in at least 2 empty test folds. Furthermore, even an 8-fold Leave-One-Gene-Out (LOGO) scheme leaves exactly one gene per test fold, where gene-specific drug resistance phenotypic shifts and transcription rates dominate variance, precluding generalizable statistical inference. Grouped evaluation on A375 is therefore marked INCOMPLETE / STATISTICALLY LIMITED.
A375.distinction_50kb_window_vs_gene_grouped: 50-kb window clustering partitions contiguous DNA segments but allows different segments of large genes (such as NF1 at 279 kb) to fall into different folds, resulting in gene-level train-validation overlap. True gene-grouped validation eliminates all intra-gene leakage, but requires a large library of diverse genes.

scientific_cautions: Locus-grouped cross-validation controls for local chromatin and epigenetic proximity within 50 kb.
Small deltas (|Delta r| <= 0.01) indicate that sequence-based model performance is not an artifact of spatial clustering.
However, this does NOT prove a 'universal sequence grammar'; cross-cell-line transfer remains restricted by cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility and assay conditions.
